name: Multiple Polyglandular Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of two or more distinct endocrine gland tumors
Histopathological confirmation of tumors from different endocrine glands
Clinical symptoms consistent with endocrine gland dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two or more distinct endocrine gland tumors confirmed histopathologically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of tumors in multiple endocrine glands

laboratory: Elevated serum calcium and parathyroid hormone levels
Abnormal fasting glucose and insulin levels
Hormonal assays indicating multiple gland hyperfunction
imaging: MRI or CT showing multiple endocrine gland tumors
Ultrasound of thyroid and parathyroid glands
Adrenal gland imaging revealing adenomas or hyperplasia
genetic: Mutations in MEN1, RET, or other polyglandular tumor-associated genes

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly parathyroid, pancreatic, and pituitary tumors
Medullary thyroid carcinoma and pheochromocytoma predominance

redFlags: Rapid onset of multiple endocrine tumors
